summary.what_changed: The issue has been rebuilt as a source-led newsletter spine: real story links first, benchmark evidence second, AI 2027 comparison third, then live media/discussion and agent handoff.
summary.trust_posture: Composite benchmark scoring stays paused. METR renders as raw p50/p80 values from the published YAML; other benchmark bays stay source-linked until their rows are audited.

news.title: Figure F.03 turned robot capability into watchable endurance evidence.
news.summary: A long public shift is more useful than another edited demo because intervention rate, recovery behavior, and task diversity become the real variables.
news.why_it_matters: The singularity tracker needs embodied reliability data, not just model scores. Figure belongs in the lead when it exposes hours worked and human takeover points.

news.title: OpenAI’s Codex enterprise promo reframed agent adoption as metering and migration.
news.summary: The primary signal is not a new model; it is a distribution wedge. Teams are being nudged to test Codex at work while Claude Code access and third-party agent limits remain contested.
news.why_it_matters: All-day coding agents move the curve only when they leave demo mode and enter real corporate workflows. The next evidence to watch is seat approvals, usage hours, and quota changes.

news.title: METR remains the autonomy anchor, but only as raw sourced data.
news.summary: The current METR Time Horizon 1.1 row puts the leading p50 estimate at 1044.78 human-expert minutes and p80 at 185.91 minutes.
news.why_it_matters: That does not authorize a smooth singularity curve. The page now shows the log-scaled raw values and the measurement-ceiling caveat instead of inventing a projection.

benchmark_panel.headline: Benchmarks are now evidence lanes, not a vibes compass.
benchmark_panel.method: Only METR is rendered as a precise chart in this issue. Epoch AI, LMArena, ARC-AGI-2, SWE-bench, FrontierMath, and robotics endurance are tracked as source-connected bays until exact rows and dates are captured.

ai_2027.original: AI 2027 treats coding automation as a core acceleration lever.
ai_2027.revision: Later AI Futures material pushes some superhuman-coder timing later than the original scenario.
ai_2027.evidence: Codex enterprise promotion is adoption evidence, not proof of superhuman coding.

ai_2027.original: The scenario depends on agents handling longer tasks with less human scaffolding.
ai_2027.revision: Timeline remains sensitive to whether measured agent horizons keep doubling.
ai_2027.evidence: METR’s leading p50 value is past a workday, but the page explicitly caveats values above 16h.

ai_2027.original: AI 2027 is mostly software-centric; physical deployment is a separate compounding lane.
ai_2027.revision: No single global score; robotics can be ahead while geopolitics or alignment remain unresolved.
ai_2027.evidence: Figure’s long live-shift format is the right evidence shape, but intervention counts still need measurement.
